title: Depth-first phase-vector collimation (Kuperberg 2013 / Regev 2004 style) for every N: O(n) qubits, time 2^((17/3) sqrt n) poly(n)

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the depth-first phase-vector collimation sieve PVSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg 2013 / Regev 2004 style collimation of low label bits, held-out parity, odd-multiplier anchored decoder; parameters l_c = ceil((3/2) sqrt n), p = l_c+2, A = 8, r, Lambda, k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability > 0.97 (in particular >= 2/3), and on every execution branch its total sequential work in the challenge model (classical bit operations, gate generation and addressing at ceil(log2(M+2)) per indexed access, exact Clifford+T gates with no synthesis, measurements, n+1 per source copy, all discarded copies, failed attempts and retries) is T(N,s) = O(2^((17/3) sqrt(n)) n^(5/2) log2 n). The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^((17/3) n^(1/2)) n^(5/2) log2 n has growth index exactly 1/2. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the outer big-O constant is absolute (independent of N, s and measurement outcomes); every exponent coefficient is an explicit rational proved in proof.md Section 8. This holds jointly with the classical-space, quantum-space and sample bounds below for the same algorithm and parameters.

For the same algorithm the depth-first phase-vector collimation sieve PVSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg 2013 / Regev 2004 style collimation of low label bits, held-out parity, odd-multiplier anchored decoder; parameters l_c = ceil((3/2) sqrt n), p = l_c+2, A = 8, r, Lambda, k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the worst-case peak classical workspace (label tables along the depth-first recursion path, measurement records, counters, parameters; no stored circuit) is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((3/2) sqrt(n)) n^(3/2)) bits. The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((3/2) n^(1/2)) n^(3/2) has growth index exactly 1/2. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the outer big-O constant is absolute (independent of N, s and measurement outcomes); every exponent coefficient is an explicit rational proved in proof.md Section 8. This holds jointly with the stated time, quantum-space and sample bounds and success probability > 0.97.

For the same algorithm the depth-first phase-vector collimation sieve PVSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg 2013 / Regev 2004 style collimation of low label bits, held-out parity, odd-multiplier anchored decoder; parameters l_c = ceil((3/2) sqrt n), p = l_c+2, A = 8, r, Lambda, k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the worst-case peak number of allocated qubits (one waiting p-qubit phase vector per recursion level, the active collimation registers, the copy-input area and O(n) ancillas) is S_Q(N,s) = O(n). The envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the big-O constant is absolute. This holds jointly with the stated time, classical-space and sample bounds and success probability > 0.97.

For the same algorithm the depth-first phase-vector collimation sieve PVSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg 2013 / Regev 2004 style collimation of low label bits, held-out parity, odd-multiplier anchored decoder; parameters l_c = ceil((3/2) sqrt n), p = l_c+2, A = 8, r, Lambda, k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including rejected labels, failed leaves, failed collimation attempts, discarded output qubits and verification tests, is at most Q_max = (n-2)*4r*16^(D_max)*8p + Lambda*k_v for n >= 16 (parameters as in proof.md Section 1) and at most N(n+6) <= 21*2^15 for n <= 15; hence Q(N,s) = O(2^((8/3) sqrt(n)) n^(3/2) log2 n). The envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((8/3) n^(1/2)) n^(3/2) log2 n has growth index exactly 1/2. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the outer big-O constant is absolute (independent of N, s and measurement outcomes); every exponent coefficient is an explicit rational proved in proof.md Section 8. This holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability > 0.97.

For the same algorithm (PVSieve of proof.md), the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability > 0.97 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
